text:
maya: heads-up — noticed a regression after the recent TS/py SDK header normalization change. some route metadata isn't reaching the console, so quota attribution looks off. :frowning:
aj: :eyes: which header specifically? route metadata should be on `x-redwood-route-meta` and we canonicalize casing in the SDK.
lucas: repro'd locally. when the SDK normalizes to `X-Redwood-Route-Meta` our internal proxy drops it because it only whitelists kebab-case `x-redwood-route-meta` in the proxy ACL. i think the normalization introduced capital letters + dash-case mismatch for our proxy checker.
priya: oof. this would explain the console showing a chunk of requests under "unknown route" and spiking quota on default buckets.
simon: can you paste the request snippet you see? also, is this only on the new TS client or py too?
maya: here's a captured outbound from the TS client (from unit test):
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.dev
X-Redwood-Route-Meta: tenant=acme;route=chat;priority=1
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
``` 
maya: proxy sees header name `X-Redwood-Route-Meta` and rejects it; earlier clients sent `x-redwood-route-meta` exactly lowercased and worked.
kate: iirc we intentionally normalized headers in SDK v2 to be consistent across platforms. but proxy whitelist logic should be agnostic to case per RFC — but our ACL code is currently doing a strict string compare. bug in proxy.
aj: filing ENG-INFRA ticket. we should patch the proxy ACL to case-fold header names and accept hyphenated names in any case. low-risk fix.
lucas: short-term mitigation: SDKs can add a compatibility shim that emits the original `x-redwood-route-meta` header in addition to the normalized one. trivial change in TS & py wrappers.
priya: i prefer patching the proxy as primary and shim as fallback. if we only ship shim, we'll keep the bug in infra.
simon: agree. plan: (1) infra fixes ACL (case-fold) — roll canary to edge proxy; (2) SDKS ship 0.0.1-hotfix that emits legacy-lower header as well; (3) console updates to display both header variants in attribution UI for two weeks and then show deprecation note.
maya: putting a quick checklist:
- infra: case-fold compare + unit tests (simon)
- devex: TS & py hotfix that duplicates header (maya/lucas)
- console: attribution UI tolerant to either header, show telemetry flag (kate)
- rollout: canary to 20% for infra, SDKs cut a patch release and opt-in canary (aj)

kate: console change: besides mapping both header names, we should add a small telemetry dimension that records which header variant was used so we can track when legacy header falls to near 0.
aj: telemetry event + metric name `route_header_variant` — values `normalized`, `legacy_lower`, `other`.
priya: also we need to check quota engine: some bucketing logic normalizes route names by lowercasing; ensure we don't double-lowercase and accidentally collide different routes.
lucas: quick test I ran: if SDK emits both headers the proxy accepts and route attribution is restored. code example in TS SDK to add in middleware:
```
req.headers['x-redwood-route-meta'] = req.headers['X-Redwood-Route-Meta'] || req.headers['x-redwood-route-meta'];
```
lucas: i'll open PR for TS now. py patch same idea.
simon: infra PR ready, adding unit tests. schedule: canary deploy tonight 23:30 UTC to edge cluster a and b at 10% each.
maya: PQ for SDK patch: we should include an explicit opt-out flag `preserve_legacy_route_header=false` default true for one release, so customers can opt into normalized-only behavior once infra is fixed.
kate: console will surface that opt-out flag in advanced settings under "client compatibility" and show a deprecation banner when we flip default in 2 weeks.
aj: small UX ask: show per-tenant timeline of header variants so support can call customers emitting legacy headers.
priya: agree — add a support-facing alert rule when a tenant spikes on `other` or `legacy_lower` after cutover.
maya: who owns the SDK release? devex will cut TS + py after PRs merge. coordinating with releases so we don't cross other breaking changes this week.
lucas: PRs: TS #4523, py #987. both target `hotfix/header-compat` branch. changelog entry: "preserve legacy route header while infra normalization rolls out".
simon: infra canary now scheduled. i'll post update when canary is healthy.
deploy-bot: [automated] infra/casefold-acl canary deploy started: 23:30 UTC -> edge cluster a (10%)
maya: thanks. once canary healthy we cut SDK patch and post release notes and console mapping timeline. :thumbsup:
kate: i'll add a small dashboard tile showing `route_header_variant` by tenant and set the alert rule.
aj: follow-ups: add an e2e test in proxy integration suite that asserts header names case-insensitive; SDK unit tests for shim; console mapping tests. back to work.
deploy-bot: [automated] infra/casefold-acl canary deploy healthy at 23:44 UTC (10% load). monitor: https://deploys.internal.redwood/cases/12345
maya: canary looks good in dashboards. cutting TS patch in 30m. will ping when artifacts are up.
lucas: py wheel uploaded to devpi. tagging release now.
maya: released TS v2.4.1-hotfix and py 1.9.2-hotfix with legacy header dual-write. changelog posted: https://go.redwood/release-notes/route-header-hotfix
priya: console mapping change deployed to staging, will land in prod tomorrow 04:00 UTC. good job team.
aj: leaving a note: follow up in two weeks to remove console banner and flip default opt-out (only after legacy header metric < 1% across active tenants).
simon: created infra ticket RN-847 to track backport to older proxies.
kate: created dashboard and alert RN-855.
maya: ok closing the thread — thanks everyone. :rocket:
